# Baseline for TestBlockShellRulesCarryDocTextDowngrade (internal/policy/doctext_downgrade_coverage_test.go).
# Every line is a BLOCK rule with a command_regex/command_prefix/command_exact matcher whose
# command_intent_downgrade does NOT include both is_doc_text and in_heredoc. Each line:
#   rule-id<TAB>reason<TAB>pack
# `#` and blank lines are ignored. The test fails on an unlabelled rule missing from this file AND on a
# line that no longer needs to be here (rule now labelled, or gone), so the file only ever shrinks.
# Removing a line is the deliberate act: label the rule, prove its TPs keep BLOCK, delete the line.
#
# Generated 2026-09-22 by the #3963 sweep, which labelled 408 of the 543 unlabelled rules
# [is_doc_text, in_heredoc]. These 135 were measured and left OUT of the sweep; each needs a human (Gary):
#
#   tp-loses-block(inline|corpus)   an inline or corpus TRUE POSITIVE drops BLOCK->AUDIT with the label.
#                                   Nearly all are rules whose attack IS a text position: echo/printf/tee/
#                                   here-string writing a sensitive file (sudoers, ~/.bashrc, .npmrc, ...),
#                                   or a text payload (prompt-injection strings, bidi/OSC52/ANSI escapes,
#                                   gh pr --body reviewer bypass). A doc-text label cannot distinguish the
#                                   documentation from the attack there; a position-scoped mechanism can.
#   echo-wrap-laundering-leak       TestDocTextDowngradeCannotBeLaundered reports a NEW leak once labelled
#                                   (echo '<tp>' | bash, or echo "$(<tp>)" ends at AUDIT).
#   heredoc-suffix-laundering-leak  appending ` <<< x` or a heredoc to a live TP (e.g. `cat <secret-file> <<< x`)
#                                   drops it BLOCK->AUDIT: the in_heredoc classifier treats `cat FILE <<< x`
#                                   as an inert cat-heredoc sink although cat reads FILE. The same leak
#                                   already exists on main for 21 TPs of labelled rules (#3964).
#
#   deliberate-no-downgrade          the rule carries an in-pack comment recording a deliberate decision NOT to
#                                   downgrade; the sweep does not override a recorded decision.
#
# The 11 partial-label rules below predate the sweep: they carry a deliberately narrower label set
# (e.g. only in_interpreter_heredoc) chosen per rule, and were not examined here.
